title: Scaling the 175B Monster: Megatron Tensor Parallelism

beats.text: Why do GPUs sit idle during LLM inference until Scaling the 175B Monster unlocks 4.5x throughput?
beats.visual_focus: A glowing 700GB data block crushing a tiny 80GB GPU die on a dark blueprint grid

beats.text: Splitting sequential layers across servers creates brutal pipeline bubbles, forcing millions of dollars of compute to sit idle waiting for activations.

beats.text: Enter Megatron tensor slicing. Instead of distributing whole layers, it cleaves individual matrix multiplications across every GPU simultaneously.

beats.text: By pairing column-parallel linear projections with row-parallel multi-head attention, GPUs compute intermediate states locally, requiring only a single all-reduce sync.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was instant fire. The contrast between needing 700GB and only having an 80GB GPU immediately grabbed me—no textbook fluff, just a brutal hardware reality. Beat 3 explains tensor parallelism cleanly without baby talk. In Beat 4, 'column-parallel linear projections with row-parallel attention blocks' is definitely a mouthful to say in 3 seconds, but tying it directly to needing just one All-Reduce sync saved it. It actually explains the core engineering trick instead of hand-waving.
